The bank estimates NVIDIA will charge about $55,000 per Rubin GPU and $5,000 per Vera CPU when sold in volume.

Morgan Stanley puts memory content per Vera Rubin rack at about $2 million, a 435% jump from the prior generation, driven by a threefold increase in LPDDR5X capacity to 54 terabytes per rack plus roughly $1 million or more in 3D NAND storage. As a share of the bill of materials, memory rose from 5-10% on the GB200 to 25-30% on the VR200, while the GPU's share fell from roughly 63% to 51%, per the Morgan Stanley bill-of-materials analysis reported by MarketScale.
A Morgan Stanley analysis reported by MarketScale says first shipments of NVIDIA's Vera Rubin rack are scheduled for the third quarter of 2026, with volume ramping in the fourth quarter.

MarketScale reports that constrained supply of DRAM, NAND and high-bandwidth memory against AI-driven demand is raising memory costs across the market, that contract DDR5 pricing has climbed sharply, and that device makers including Samsung and Apple are expected to pass higher memory costs into upcoming products.

Morgan Stanley notes that procurement structure can move NVIDIA's final rack pricing by more than $1 million per rack, and that a hyperscaler self-sourcing certain memory modules could bring the Vera Rubin rack price down to around $6.7 million, per MarketScale.
